what: The page says Node words the bad-JSON error differently from Chromium, quoting a Node message that Node does not actually print.
evidence: Panel 21 readlist: "That's Chromium's wording. Node says Unexpected token 'o', "[object Object]" is not valid JSON for the same mistake". No capture backs this. Run in scratch with /opt/node22 (v22.23.4), /opt/node24 (v24.22.1) and /opt/node26 (v26.13.0): `JSON.parse("[object Object]")` prints `"[object Object]" is not valid JSON` on all three, the same as the captured Chromium line (storage_parse.html stderr). V8 uses the 'Unexpected token' form only for other text, e.g. `JSON.parse("[object")` gives `Unexpected token 'o', "[object" is not valid JSON`. The Version notes page also lists `"[object Object]" is not valid JSON` as Chromium-only wording.
fix: Replace the second readlist item with: "Node (the same V8 engine) prints exactly the same message." Or capture a Node program and quote that. In the Version notes, drop `"[object Object]" is not valid JSON` from the Chromium-only list.

what: The example doesn't fit the rule it illustrates. It speaks of an O(n) algorithm losing to an O(n^2) one, but TimSort's case is insertion sort (O(n^2)) beating merge sort (O(n log n)).
evidence: "It also means an O(n) algorithm with a big constant can lose to an O(n²) one on small inputs, which is exactly why TimSort uses insertion sort for short runs."
fix: "...a faster-growing algorithm with small constants can beat a slower-growing one on small inputs: that's why TimSort uses insertion sort (O(n²)) instead of merging for short runs."
